messages:
sahil: Heads up — noticed a p95 jump on small requests after last runtime change, looks tied to KV reuse across requests. cc @jess @maria :eyes:

jess: Saw that too. Short prompts p95 went ~18ms -> ~36ms. Any profiler dumps?

perf-bot: profile summary for 5234012345: kv_lookup p95 22ms -> 49ms, allocs spike during longctx sessions. flamegraph: https://perf.redwood/internal/fg/5234012345 (restricted)

maria: Quick observation: we switched prefix fingerprint from Murmur -> xxh3 in commit 9f3. Could change collision / bucket distribution. Current cache key format: 
``
cache_key = tenant_id + ":" + model + ":" + prefix_hash
``

sahil: We added fingerprinting to shorten keys and avoid long string copies. But if collision pattern changed, we might be getting extra equality checks and memcmp thrash when many sessions hit same prefix -> page churn.

jess: Can we bisect whether this is kernel selection/batching change vs KV keying? I noticed a kernel selector tweak (split-kernel for short seqs) landed around same time. Might affect memory access patterns too.

runtime-oncall: I can repro on canary, need a minimal repro command. @sahil can you paste your load command and approximate env?

sahil: repro command we used locally:
``
# simple HTTP loadtest
ab -n 500 -c 10 -p payload.json -T application/json http://canary.internal/v1/generate
# internal runner
python perf/loadtest.py --model "redwood-llama-13b" --prefix "Q: " --sessions 50 --seq 64 --duration 60
``

perf-bot: stack sample (hot): runtime::kv::lookup -> runtime::kv::page_fault_handler -> runtime::mem::copy -> kernel::split_attention

maria: Looking at traces: fragmentation pattern is subtle — longctx sessions allocate pages and eviction is per-page LRU but keys get rehashed across buckets during compaction -> many small holes. Two quick mitigations: 1) periodic page compaction/defrag, 2) prefer placing sticky prefixes into contiguous slabs (sticky placement).

jess: Also architectural idea: include an optional `session_hint` in cache key when session affinity is expected. Today key = tenant:model:prefix which causes multiple sessions sharing same prefix to collide on same key and thrash. Proposal: key = tenant:model:prefix[:session_hint] where session_hint appended only if caller sets `X-Session-Sticky` or if session request count > threshold. Tradeoff: less cross-request reuse for truly shared prefixes.

sahil: That tradeoff seems ok if we gate by session activity. A/B plan: enable session_hint for sessions with >5 requests; otherwise use global prefix key. Also enable compaction every 5m and measure.

runtime-oncall: I'll wire canary rollout with feature flags: `kv.session_hint_threshold=5`, `kv.compaction_interval_secs=300`. Will run the internal loadtest and capture p50/p95 and kv metrics.

jess: Need better telemetry before/after: add counters for `kv.prefix_hits`, `kv.session_sticky_hits`, `kv.page_frag_ratio`, and histogram for `kv.key_cmp_count` (number of memcmp/equality checks per lookup).

perf-bot: Metrics PR queued — will emit `kv.prefix_hits`, `kv.session_sticky_hits`, `kv.page_frag_ratio`, `kv.key_cmp_count` in next prod roll.

maria: One more note: kernel selector change could amplify memcopy hotspots because split-kernel introduces different attn buffer lifetimes. If compaction reduces fragmentation, split-kernel side-effects will be smaller. We should test combos: (split-kernel on/off) x (session_hint on/off) x (compaction interval).

sahil: I'll open a small RFC with the plan + rollback steps and link loadtest results. TL;DR: try session_hint gated by request-count + periodic compaction; measure p95 & resident mem over 10m runs.

jess: Sounds good. Thanks everyone — assign follow-ups? @runtime-oncall will run canary, @maria will prototype sticky placement, @sahil to draft RFC. :thumbsup:
